prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view of a floor workspace where the camera wearer sits or crouches with limbs in the bright foreground (0.3–0.6 m away), looking down at two circular metal plates on the left and center (~0.7–1.0 m away, ~0.1–0.2 m apart) and an elevated gas stove supporting a wok on the right (~0.5–0.9 m away). Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer's arms reach forward and shift between the plates and the stove, while a second person on the upper-left approaches from the background (~1.2 m in frames 1–3) into the foreground (~0.6–0.8 m in frames 4–5) to reach the central vegetable plate, with both people's heads out of view and all floor items within arm's reach of both individuals. The map makes the 3D elevation of the wok, stove, and reaching arms above the flat floor plane much clearer than the dimly lit RGB image, and clearly separates the foreground limbs occluding the floor and bowls. However, it looks unreliable inside the concave, reflective metal dishes—where the hollow interiors appear flat or artificially deep—and along the blurred depth boundaries of the fast-moving arms in frame 3.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies parts of the camera wearer's limbs in the lower foreground (0.3–0.7 m away), the second person's limbs entering from the left (0.6–1.2 m away), and the central metal plates labeled as 'bowl' (0.7–1.0 m away) within arm's reach on the floor. Across the 5 frames, it tracks the spatial shift from the wearer's isolated lower limbs in frame 1 to both people's arms converging on the central bowl in frame 5, though bodies and heads remain cropped out of the frame so gaze and full body orientation cannot be determined from masks alone. While it helps isolate the circular boundaries of the central food bowls and foreground limb silhouettes from the dark background in frames 2, 3, and 5, the map is highly unreliable and inconsistent across time. It completely misses the plates and stove in frames 1 and 4, misclassifies the floor in frame 3 as a 'dining table', merges the wearer's right arm with the gas stove into a single 'person' mask in frame 2, and merges the second person's limbs with the left plate in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the 5 frames, detecting only a single magenta right-hand skeleton for the camera wearer in frames 2 and 5 at roughly 0.5–0.7 m distance in the lower-right quadrant, with no yellow body skeletons detected at all. In frame 2, the detected hand is positioned just left of the gas stove holding a utensil above the floor, and in frame 5 it is angled toward the central vegetable plate within arm's reach, showing a slight inward rotation and leftward shift between those two moments. When present, the 3D finger and palm keypoints show the exact grasp articulation of the wearer's right hand holding the spoon, which is difficult to resolve in the dark, motion-blurred RGB frames. However, the map is largely unreliable for broader spatial understanding because heavy self-occlusion, crop truncation of heads and torsos, and low lighting cause it to miss all body poses, the wearer's left hand, the right hand in frames 1, 3, and 4, and all limbs of the second person approaching on the left.
